correctness.rationale: After symmetry reduction to \(t=b/a\in[0,1]\), sign averaging gives exactly \(\mathbb E|a\varepsilon_1R_1+b\varepsilon_2R_2|=a\mathbb E\max(R_1,tR_2)\). The expectation has two explicit branches separated at \(c=(1-d)/(1+d)\). The first decreases, the second has a single interior maximum, so only \(c\) and \(1\) can minimize. Their exact squared difference has sign \(d(d^3+4d^2+d-4)\), and the cubic has one root in \((0,1)\) because its derivative is positive there. Boundary and uniqueness cases are included.
